chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub from Hisham ibn Salim from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every Muslim, in the presence of two other Muslims, who reneges from Islam and denies the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and belies him, then his blood is permissible for anyone who hears that from him, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him on the day he reneges, so do not approach her, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him, and he does not ask him to repent.'
ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences for an apostate in Shia Islam according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the distinct Shia ruling of 'Qatl bi-l-Ghayr' (execution by others) for the apostate, emphasizing that the Imam holds the authority to execute without the customary period of inviting repentance (istitab). It further clarifies the immediate legal consequences, including the irrevocable separation of the wife and the distribution of wealth, reflecting the severity of publicly denying Prophethood. This view is often contrasted with the Sunni perspective which typically requires a waiting period for repentance before execution.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Every Muslim, in between two Muslims reneges from Al-Islam (becomes an apostate), and denies Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> of his<sup>saww</sup> Prophet-hood, and belies him<sup>saww</sup>. So his blood is Permissible to be shed for every one who hears that from him, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him the day he reneges, so she cannot go near him, and his wealth is distributed upon his inheritors, and his wife would observe the waiting period of the one widowed from her husband, and it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he kills him, and does not give him (the opportunity) to repent’.
